changes: No changes: the chronogram netra(2) veda(4) adri(7) bhū(1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1742 = c. 1820 CE; no human persons named (Viśveśvara is a deity).

notes: The catalogue gives ŚS 1509, but the chronogram netravedādribhū (2-4-7-1, read right to left) gives Śaka 1742, about 1820 CE. The catalogue field looks wrong. The rest of the colophon line has a gap ('----') and a garbled 'vadatipustakam', so a scribe's or owner's name may be lost there. 'śrīviśveśvaraprasādāt' invokes a deity (Viśveśvara), not a person. The colophon itself reads 'iti varṣataṃtraṃ samāptam', which names the Varṣatantra, a section of the Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī.
